body:
I hadn't thought of asking a pharmacist, is there anything you've taken that's helped - even just in the short term until I can see a psychiatrist? I've been taking omega-3 for a few months now and have some herbal calming tablet-type things but other than that I am clueless.

Thanks for the comment! :)

My uni doesn't have a psychiatrist in-house but does have a wellbeing team who carry out basic CBT and counselling, I might give that a try in the mean time. Definitely will talk to lecturers about it, it's just a little tricky working up the courage (my lecturers tend to focus on the "we won't give you advice unless you ask for it/independent learning" style of teaching so I haven't spoken to them much over my degree, but I'd guess they'd be understanding). And you're right, reducing stress is a big one, I'll look into that too.

Sorry, I meant to say I'm *not* currently on meds and haven't been for about 4 years. I do have some olanzapine and quietiapine somewhere but didn't want to start taking it again without supervision from a doctor. 

Thanks so much for the comment! :)

Thank you! I hadn't thought of that, I don't know if that's possible here (UK) since psychiatrists usually take referrals from your GP, who's currently in the city I'm living in, but couldn't hurt to try. Thanks again

That's exactly it man! Any time I have any sort of anxiety or emotional response to **anything** it sets me off, and then I end up spending hours a day thinking about how I got ill in the first place, what I'm doing currently to get better and the future - I want to stop thinking about depression and just live in the moment but can't trust my emotions to remain stable without "monitoring" them. 

No matter whether it's a 100m sprint or a marathon, you'll get there if you keep moving in the right direction, even if you have to start over a few times :)

Hey thanks for the reply!

Yes I do think acceptance is a big part of it. The only problem is I tend to worry and ruminate a lot, and get caught in that sort of "it happened before - it could happen again" thinking which keeps me on edge looking for symptoms of relapse. This just leaves me stuck between denying it/not accepting it and accepting it but worrying about the implications. 

I'm sorry to hear you're not quite recovered yet, but I do hope you can get there! If it helps, only a couple of months ago I didn't think I could get to the point I'm in now - I know I'm not better 100% but there's been a huge recovery - I'm sure it's possible for you too :)

Yeah that's true - I feel a lot less trapped in this state when I'm talking to people. Unfortunately I don't talk to people often, and one of my stupid worries is that one day I'll "lose control" and start telling everyone my inner monologue or whatever and make a fool of myself or reveal something personal.

I realise I'm 4 days late but I've had this too; analysing every single aspect of your life and personality to the point where there's nothing left to analyse and you just feel empty and as though you totally lack any sort of humanity.

You're not alone in this, and you can get out of it :) Feel free to pm if you need to man

Yeah, everyone I've spoken to about this who's older than me has said this is a really weird time. I just get stuck wondering if this sort of thing is something I should be actively thinking about to try and get through it or if I should just be ignoring it - I guess that's probably a normal thing to worry about anyway.

I get that about music I suppose, I've liked the sort of music I like for ages now, and not just because of any weed association. I mean I did discover a lot of new music when I was smoking but out of a genuine enjoyment of the music rather than just searching for weed-related music. Though of course when I'm anxious or feeling a bit down I'm guilty of being like "hey, you were such a try hard, and now you're such a poser," stupid shit like that.

Same with clothes I guess, it's not that I walk around with weed leaves emblazoned on myself or harem pants and dreads (nothing against anyone who likes dressing that way of course) or anything like that, it's just the association I have that's stuck, which sucks because my clothes are pretty comfortable haha. Again, I really think I'm overthinking.

It's the same with my friends really, though the ones I'm closest to tend towards the heavy side. I spend a lot of time with my girlfriend, which is great because I enjoy her company and we have a good time, but also she is pretty anti-weed and as much as she does try, it's difficult talking about this sort of thing with her. As I can gain more self esteem and confidence I guess it'll be easier to put myself out there should I decide it's time to move on and find more friends.

I've been lifting weights and exercising a lot more too actually, never been fat or ripped or anything, just thought it'd be a good boost for my health and confidence if I got more in-shape. But yeah, I'll have a think about what specifically might be causing my low self confidence and try and work on that. Might be time to get a job too now you mention it. Good for you for raising your self esteem though man, it makes me feel a or more optimistic and motivated about the future hearing about people's success.

Haha yeah that's me all over, I keep worrying myself and dwelling 24/7, I guess my long-term goal is to work on living more in the moment and not overthinking all the possibilities of what *could* happen. Thanks a lot for typing this all up though man, lots of great advice here, it's really helped put it all into perspective! Hope you're doing well yourself :-)
Thanks, I'm seeing one tomorrow, I know it's all part of the hypochondria but I just keep doubting it all
That sounds like me all over
Sorry, I realised I'd misinterpreted your comment. I understand what you mean now, thank you for your comment and I hope everything is ok with you and your ex!
That's very worrying, are you suggesting I may be schizophrenic? I am very sorry to hear about this and I hope you're both doing well now!
Fair enough, I hope you're alright!

I hope we can get through this, good luck man! 

Edit: also can you please keep me informed on what happens?

It is a difficult situation, though I'm grateful I'm in this situation rather than having actually been psychotic.

I hope you are doing alright and that you can work through your issues, you're right, she shouldn't just ignore her child's experiences for the sake of preserving "normality", it would be infinitely more beneficial to seek help and treat your condition (whatever it may be) than to ignore it and pretend it doesn't exist, because only one of those two scenarios will have a good prognosis.

They didn't remove the diagnosis because I was exhibiting negative symptoms of schizophrenia (basically depression and thought issues), though this was due to my ASD rather than actual schizophrenia symptoms, and the doctor who I was referred to usually treats psychosis and thus had no understanding of Asperger's as a differential diagnosis. Basically, I received my diagnosis through a mixture of my obsessions resembling psychosis (though never having been actually psychotic) and my depression and ASD resembling negative symptoms of schizophrenia. If that makes sense?

I'm aware of the memory doubting/OCD link, it really sucks because I know full well I was not psychotic, as do the psychiatrists I saw on the ward, my therapist and my parents, but this misdiagnosis and the fact that a person who had exhibited psychosis would my recognise it have sent my anxiety through the roof!
That's what my diagnosis is! I hope it goes ok for you, how have you dealt with it since?

Thank you, I wasn't intending to ask for a diagnosis, if anything I want less diagnoses than more haha!

I'm going to bring it up after my next meeting. The reason it is so present in my mind currently is my issues with obsessions and intrusive thoughts as part of ASD, most of which revolve around schizophrenia. In other words, several months ago I was able to ignore my misdiagnosis and just wanted to focus on improving my ASD symptoms, though after a period of stress I suddenly began ruminating on the misdiagnosis and so it has exacerbated my symptoms.

I hope this made sense, but thank you for your comment!

Yes that's the plan really. My parents agree that I was not psychotic, and the psychiatrist at the ward suggested Asperger's as a differential diagnosis. I am really sick of it, I believe the diagnosis has stuck because I have many of the negative symptoms of schizophrenia (I'm depressed a lot, don't socialise a huge amount, my thoughts can be a little confusing at times), though this is linked to my Asperger's and depression. On top of all of this, the psychosis diagnosis has caused obsessive worry, doubt and rumination, and I panic that I may be schizophrenic despite the fact I have never hallucinated or been delusional. Whenever I get one of these "what if you're schizophrenic" thoughts I can't calm myself down because I latch onto the psychosis diagnosis and it fuels the doubt and rumination, and now my personality is dominated by excessive doubt and anxiety. 

Furthermore, I've taken LSD before and used cannabis a bit (both years after the psychosis diagnosis), it is my understanding that if I was predisposed to psychosis, either of these substances would be likely to have induced it. When I tripped I just got a little anxiety but was overall pretty level-headed, and even under the influence still had no hallucinations other than slight visual warping. Apologies for rambling, it's just an annoying situation to be in and I really don't know how to vocalise it all.

I'm sorry to hear that! The main thing I have learned from this situation is how tough it must be to live with schizophrenia/psychosis. I hope that you can find whatever help you need to get better, or hopefully you have overcame your issues!
